boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Staunton River Bridge record (June 25, 1864) in the Richmond-Petersburg Campaign [June 1864-March 1865]. The Wilson-Kautz raid of June 22-July 1 contains three frozen records: Staunton River Bridge (VA113, June 25), Sappony Church (VA067, June 28) and Reams' Station (VA068, June 29). Army-wide returns, raid-wide and multi-action loss totals, and the siege as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force text reads 'Divisions (4,000 total)' and the live field zero. Wilson's February 1865 report says the expedition set out with about 5,500 cavalry and twelve guns and found the bridge defended by 500 or 600 men and a battery of six guns; his July 3, 1864 report says the militia of eight counties and a small force from Danville.
claims.rationale: Wilson's 5,500 is the raid's starting strength on June 22 and his defender figure an estimate; the frozen 4,000 is undivided. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory. Lee says the enemy was signally repulsed at the bridge and retreated; Wilson says Kautz had to give up the attempt, and that the expedition's objects had in the main been accomplished.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Wilson's claim concerns the raid as a whole, not this record.

open_questions: Kautz's report (No. 280), the reports of Kautz's brigade commanders, W. H. F. Lee's and Farinholt's reports, and Humphreys' raid passage (pp.236-241; read, not selected under the three-family ceiling) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, later commander of its Second Corps, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; it relies on Meade's, Hancock's, Warren's, Burnside's, Parke's and Wilson's reports and quotes Lee's, Beauregard's and Gordon's despatches, so it is not independent of those families. Gillmore's, Meade's, Hancock's, Burnside's, Wilson's, Hampton's, Stannard's and Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volumes XXXVI (Part 2), XL, XLII and XLVI (Part 1), are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; each volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Lee's telegrams largely relay subordinates' reports. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
